name: Question 6
problem: A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis. When the displacement of $P$ from the origin is $x\,m,$ the velocity is $v\,m/s,$ the magnitude of the acceleration is $kx\,{m/s}^{2},$ where $k$ is a positive constant, and the acceleration is directed toward $O.$ If $P$ has velocity $v=6\,m/s$ at the origin and the particle is at rest when its displacement is $3\sqrt{2}\,m,$ find the value of $k.$
worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094290/assets/cd42eb74e5bba02951118c349a1b25f7193c39aa53f6504403918dfa984eb2c2.png)

Since the acceleration of the particle $P$ has magnitude $kx\,{m/s}^{2}$ and is directed *toward* $O,$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=-kx.
$$

Using the fact that

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}),
$$

we can rewrite our equation as

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})=-kx.
$$

Integrating both sides of the above equation with respect to $x,$ we have

$$
\int \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})\text{d}x=\int (-kx)\,\text{d}x
$$

which gives the general solution

$$
\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}=-\frac{k}{2}{x}^{2}+C.
$$

Now, since $v=6\,m/s$ when $x=0\,m,$ we can find the value of the constant $C,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & =-\frac{k}{2}{x}^{2}+C \\ \frac{1}{2}(6)^{2} & =-\frac{k}{2}(0)^{3}+C \\ C & =18\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}=18-\frac{k}{2}{x}^{2}.
$$

Finally, since $v=0\,m/s$ when $x=3\sqrt{2}\,m,$ we can find the value of the positive constant $k,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & =18-\frac{k}{2}{x}^{2} \\ \frac{1}{2}(0)^{2} & =18-\frac{k}{2}(3\sqrt{2})^{2} \\ 18-9k & =0 \\ 9k & =18 \\ k & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 6

A particle P moves along the x-axis. When the displacement of P from the origin is xm, the velocity is vm/s, the magnitude of the acceleration is kxm/s2, where k is a positive constant, and the acceleration is directed toward O. If P has velocity v=6m/s at the origin and the particle is at rest when its displacement is 32m, find the value of k.

b

c

Correct
EXPLANATION

Since the acceleration of the particle P has magnitude kxm/s2 and is directed toward O, we have

dvdt=−kx.

Using the fact that dvdt=ddx(12v2), we can rewrite our equation as

ddx(12v2)=−kx.

Integrating both sides of the above equation with respect to x, we have

∫ddx(12v2)dx=∫(−kx)dx

which gives the general solution

12v2=−k2x2+C.

Now, since v=6m/s when x=0m, we can find the value of the constant C, as follows:

12v2=−k2x2+C12(6)2=−k2(0)3+CC=18

Therefore,

12v2=18−k2x2.

Finally, since v=0m/s when x=32m, we can find the value of the positive constant k, as follows:

12v2=18−k2x212(0)2=18−k2(32)218−9k=09k=18k=2.
